standard_prerequisites.name: The Chern character identifies K theory with rational Chow groups
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Chow Homology, the lemma giving the isomorphism from the Grothendieck group tensored with the rationals to the rational Chow ring via the Chern character capped with the fundamental class, and the remark that it is a ring isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the isomorphism through which the cycle class map is defined from the Chern character of the cohomology theory.

standard_prerequisites.name: Compatibility of the Chern character with pullbacks
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma on the Chern character of the cohomology theory, and Chow Homology, the remark on compatibility of Chern classes with pullbacks
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the constructed cycle class map is compatible with pullbacks.

standard_prerequisites.name: The second Adams operator and the grading of the Chern character
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Chow Homology, the lemma on the second Adams operator and its action on classes in a fixed codimension, together with the lemma relating the Adams operators to the Chern character of the cohomology theory
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the cycle class map is graded, i.e. that classes of codimension i land in the cohomological degree 2i.

core_obligations: Define the map (proof lines 4716-4728): the Chern character capped with the fundamental class gives an isomorphism of rings from the rational Grothendieck group to the rational Chow ring; define the cycle class map of a cycle as the Chern character of the cohomology theory evaluated at the unique K theory class whose Chern character capped with the fundamental class is that cycle.

Compatibility with pullbacks (proof lines 4728-4734): both the Chern character of the cohomology theory and the passage from K theory to Chow groups are compatible with pullbacks, so the constructed map is compatible with pullbacks as well.

Gradedness (proof lines 4734-4758): the second Adams operator acts on the K theory class corresponding to a cycle of codimension i by multiplication by the i-th power of two, which by the relation between the Adams operators and the Chern character of the cohomology theory shows that the value of the cycle class map on that cycle lies in cohomological degree twice the codimension, which completes the proof.
proof_roadmap: Use the Chern character isomorphism to define the cycle class map.
Use the second Adams operator to show the map is graded.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that given the data and the first four axioms there is a unique rule assigning to every smooth projective scheme a graded ring homomorphism from the rational Chow ring to the sum of the even twists of the cohomology, compatible with pullbacks and intertwining the classical Chern character with the Chern character of the theory (statement lines 4712-4721). The proof (proof lines 4722-4758) defines the map through the isomorphism between K theory and Chow groups, checks pullback compatibility, and uses the second Adams operator for gradedness. H3: a construction with a gradedness argument through Adams operations, written out in full.
